exceptions.justification: A pointer to the SARIF 2.1.0 specification in the shipped type declarations; it documents the shape of the SARIF log data-cap emits.
exceptions.alternatives: Reword the comment to name the version without a link; consumers lose the direct pointer to the specification the types implement.
exceptions.attempted: Considered rewording the declaration comment without a link.
exceptions.constraint: The link is the most useful single pointer for someone reading the SARIF types; a version number alone sends them searching.
exceptions.remediation: None needed; revisit with the SARIF types.
exceptions.residualRisk: One informational supply-chain alert; no behaviour.
exceptions.revisitWhen: the SARIF types are next changed, or Socket stops reporting urlStrings.
exceptions.ruleBroken: DistNoUrls: no scheme-prefixed URL may ship in the build output unexplained (Socket.dev urlStrings alert).
exceptions.whyPreferable: A documentation link in a type comment costs one informational Socket alert and nothing at runtime.

exceptions.justification: The documentation link inside the Evidence Model note stamped into generated Markdown reports; it tells the reader of a report where the model is explained.
exceptions.alternatives: Name the file without a scheme (github.com/MaverickCER/data-cap/...), which is not clickable in a rendered report.
exceptions.attempted: Considered dropping the link and citing internal ADR numbers instead; that was the audit finding (ADRs are meaningless to the report's audience).
exceptions.constraint: A reader of a generated report needs a working link, and a Markdown report renders it as one.
exceptions.residualRisk: One informational supply-chain alert; no behaviour.
exceptions.revisitWhen: a stable documentation site replaces the repository path.
exceptions.ruleBroken: DistNoUrls: no scheme-prefixed URL may ship in the build output unexplained (Socket.dev urlStrings alert).
exceptions.whyPreferable: A clickable link is the entire point of the note.

exceptions.constraint: A relative path is wrong for every user of the published package; an absolute URL is right.
exceptions.residualRisk: One informational supply-chain alert; no behaviour.
exceptions.revisitWhen: the help text is reworked or a documentation site exists.

exceptions.justification: The `meta.docs.url` of each data-cap ESLint rule, built from the rule name; ESLint's convention uses it so editors link to the rule's documentation.
exceptions.alternatives: Omit `meta.docs.url` (optional in ESLint); editors lose the per-rule documentation link.
exceptions.constraint: ESLint tooling surfaces `meta.docs.url` directly to users who hit a rule violation.
exceptions.remediation: Decided: keep. The per-rule link is the documented ESLint convention and the cost is one informational alert.
exceptions.residualRisk: One informational supply-chain alert; no behaviour.
exceptions.revisitWhen: the plugin is split into its own package or ESLint drops the convention.
exceptions.ruleBroken: DistNoUrls: no scheme-prefixed URL may ship in the build output unexplained (Socket.dev urlStrings alert).
exceptions.whyPreferable: A direct link from a lint error to its explanation is worth one informational alert.

exceptions.justification: The `informationUri` of the SARIF tool driver data-cap reports, which SARIF consumers show as the tool's documentation link.
exceptions.alternatives: Omit `informationUri` (optional in SARIF); consumers lose the link.
exceptions.constraint: Code-scanning UIs show this as the tool's home.
exceptions.remediation: Decided: keep, for the same reason as the rule links.
exceptions.residualRisk: One informational supply-chain alert; no behaviour.
exceptions.ruleBroken: DistNoUrls: no scheme-prefixed URL may ship in the build output unexplained (Socket.dev urlStrings alert).

exceptions.justification: The `$schema` value of every SARIF log data-cap emits. It is the conventional, validator-friendly identifier for SARIF 2.1.0; consumers and editors use it to validate the log.
exceptions.alternatives: Omit `$schema`: SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.13.3 makes it optional, so the log stays valid, but editors lose schema-aware validation and completion.
exceptions.attempted: Checked the specification: `$schema` is optional (an earlier version of this record wrongly said it was required).
exceptions.constraint: Ecosystem convention rather than a specification requirement: validators and editors key off the URL.
exceptions.remediation: Decided: keep. Not required by the specification, but it is what GitHub's own examples and every validator expect.
exceptions.residualRisk: One informational supply-chain alert; no behaviour.
exceptions.revisitWhen: consumers stop relying on `$schema` for SARIF validation.
exceptions.ruleBroken: DistNoUrls: no scheme-prefixed URL may ship in the build output unexplained (Socket.dev urlStrings alert).
exceptions.whyPreferable: Emitting the conventional identifier keeps the log self-describing for every consumer.
